claim: Popover (172 lines, 15 tests) has no production importer and its doc names Multi Install, which uses Dialog; 13 of 26 icons have no importer (no bundle cost: they are /* @__PURE__ */); Listbox props estimateSize and overscan are unused; InstalledSection re-exports rules used only by a test; 9 rendered class names have no CSS rule, one of them (.nuiget-tab-label) is an ExTester hook outside §8.
proposal: Delete or adopt Popover with the context-menu decision; prune unused icons and props in the refactor items.

claim: ARCHITECTURE says ConfirmDialog covers remove source over Source Settings, but the code uses an inline role=group confirmation; Dialog's doc comment says the page is not dimmed although a scrim exists since P9.11.
proposal: Fix in the first refactor item that touches Dialog or Sources.

claim: When the installed version is chosen, the details primary button shows a disabled 'Update'. The reason ('This version is installed') is only a tooltip, because the note is suppressed for that case. The model also lists Uninstall among the primary labels, but Uninstall is always a separate button.
proposal: Define the label and enablement of the details actions for each installed and chosen version combination.

claim: State announcements and busy semantics drift from the model. The main panel never announces the first load, because Skeleton is aria-hidden and only the sidebar announces its installed list. Revalidation puts aria-busy on the listbox, not on rows. The sidebar's provisional explanation is a span title that screen readers do not read, while the main panel's Badge title is read. Sidebar All Projects headers have no provisional or Unsupported badge.
proposal: Fix one vocabulary for loading, revalidating and provisional, with the same ARIA on both surfaces.

claim: Microcopy is inconsistent although the terminology is clean ('feed' never appears; 'remove' is used only for sources). Inconsistencies: casing ('All sources' vs 'All Sources'; 'Include prerelease' vs 'Include Pre-release'); three variants of the sources-unavailable banner; filter-empty sentences in singular and plural; 'Author(s)' vs 'Authors:'; the panel named 'full view', 'Full Manager' and 'Manage NuGet packages'; key hints that differ for the same list and always say Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter); toast prepositions ('Uninstalled X from P' vs 'Uninstall of X in P failed'); host messages without the 'nUIget:' prefix; downloads shown as '9325.4M'; the CPM install preview confirming with 'Update central version'.
proposal: Write one microcopy table (nouns, casing, empty, error and unavailable sentences, hint grammar) and lint it.

claim: Browse has no paging or 'load more' (at most searchResultLimit, default 20, maximum 100) and lists nothing on an empty query. Visual Studio's Browse shows popular packages; NuGet Gallery pages on scroll.
proposal: 1.5 d contract change (skip or a cursor on search/query). A stable second page over results merged from several sources needs a cursor per source.

claim: An existing source cannot be edited (URL, name, credentials, insecure flag); a user has to remove and re-add it. Visual Studio Options and Rider both edit sources.
proposal: 1 d contract change: add a sources/update request backed by `dotnet nuget update source` (fits ADR-003; the command was not verified in this session). Watch DPAPI passwords and renames that break mappings.

claim: There is no licence-acceptance prompt for packages that require it, no in-editor licence text for embedded licence files, and no warning when an update changes the licence. Visual Studio prompts and has a View License dialog; Averenium warns on licence changes.
proposal: 1–1.5 d contract change (requireLicenseAcceptance and licence fields on PackageMetadata). Not verified whether `dotnet package add` enforces acceptance.

claim: The details pane lacks owners (Visual Studio 17.11 shows profile links), tags (NuGet Gallery), release notes (the Extensions view exemplar has a Changelog section) and a link to the package's page on its source.
proposal: 0.5–1 d. Owners, tags and releaseNotes need domain.ts fields (D6). A nuget.org package-page link needs none.

claim: There are no update policies: no patch/minor/major label on update rows, no 'skip majors' in Update all, no per-package ignore or pin, no cool-down for freshly published versions. nifty, NuGet Compass, ManagedCode, Averenium and sockless offer these; the Extensions view has a per-item Auto Update toggle.
proposal: Semver-delta label: 0.25 d, webview only. Ignore list: 1 d (persisted state; probably a protocol change).

claim: Only the HTTP cache can be cleared. Visual Studio clears http-cache, global-packages, temp and plugins-cache; Rider's Folders tab shows sizes and clears selected caches.
proposal: 0.25–0.5 d, no protocol change: a QuickPick over `dotnet nuget locals <kind> --clear`.

claim: There is no preview of the full change and no dependency-behaviour options; nUIget previews CPM impact only. Visual Studio's Show preview window, Dependency behavior and File conflict options mostly apply to project types other than SDK PackageReference.
proposal: Do not plan this. Record it as a deliberate scope limit.

claim: No keybinding is contributed to open the manager or focus the sidebar. The Extensions view uses Ctrl+Shift+X; Rider uses Alt+Shift+7.
proposal: 0.1 d: choose an unbound chord, or document the existing view-focus command. Check for collisions first.

claim: The UI is English only (D11). C# Dev Kit localizes its manifest strings, and Nuggy ships four UI languages.
proposal: Deferred by D11; noted, not scored. Manifest nls 0.5 d; webview strings 3–5 d.

claim: Offered versions are not filtered by the project's target framework, so an update can target only a newer TFM. NuGet Compass and Nuggy filter or label by compatibility; Visual Studio was not verified.
proposal: 2–3 d, high risk (a framework-compatibility reducer in TypeScript). Not for 2.0.x.

proposal: Resolve through the sidebar vulnerability-mark finding (render the data) rather than by removing the request.

claim: Parity rows MI10 and MU8 are still open: no Collapse all / Expand all on the Installed and All Projects Updates toolbars.
proposal: 0.5 d each, no protocol change.

proposal: 0.5 d each, no protocol change.

claim: Parity row MI12 is partly closed: All Projects headers always show the count and have no hover background.
proposal: 0.25 d. Visual-dimension overlap; the owner chooses.

claim: Parity row MB16 is still open: after the prerelease toggle the version selector keeps its previous version, and the version list is unbounded.
proposal: 0.25 d, no protocol change.

claim: Parity row MB17 is still open: HTML entities in search and registration descriptions are shown literally. Whether any feed actually sends them was not verified.
proposal: 0.25 d, no protocol change.

claim: Parity row MB18 is still open: ArrowLeft and ArrowRight in the package list no longer switch the Details and README tabs.
proposal: 0.5 d, no protocol change.

claim: Parity row MB19 is still open: the first Browse load announces nothing, contrary to interaction-model §4.
proposal: 0.25 d. Hand to the accessibility dimension.

claim: Parity row SB10 is still open: the sidebar's All Projects project headers carry no provisional badge.
proposal: 0.25 d, no protocol change.

claim: Parity row SB13 is still open: the sidebar section count shows 0 and sits beside the spinner. This was a deliberate 2.0 choice that a test asserts.
proposal: Owner choice, 0.1 d.

claim: Parity row SB14 is still open: the sidebar search box is focused only on the ui/focusSearch event, not on first render.
proposal: 0.1 d, no protocol change.

claim: Persisted state is split three ways. The main split is in globalState through layout/*, the session is in workspaceState, and the tab, the sidebar sections and the sidebar split are in webview state. The protocol's sidebarSectionSplit has no reader or writer in either webview. No WebviewPanelSerializer is registered, so the main panel is not restored after a window reload. The sidebar's webview state is saved with the view. Section collapse, filters and per-surface density can persist with no contract change.
proposal: Keep new surface-local preferences in webview state. Consider a panel serializer (host-only) if restoring the panel after a reload matters.

claim: On a hovered row, contrast drops below 4.5:1 in some themes (computed). The new-version colour measures 4.36 in Light Modern, 4.09 in Light 2026 and 3.98 in Light+. Muted text in the sidebar measures 4.16 in Dark 2026 and 3.98 in Light+. The tokens.css comment quotes ratios on the editor background only, and the theme pass never hovers.
proposal: Measure a hovered row in the theme pass (H7). If the failure holds, revert secondary text to inherit on hover, as the selected-row rule does.

claim: When a list empties, focus moves to the .nuiget-listbox-empty container, which has outline: none and no role. Sighted keyboard users then lose the focus indicator.
proposal: Draw the shared focus ring on the empty container, or move focus to the list's section toggle.

claim: Links in the details facts and the README have no nUIget focus rule and take VS Code's webview default outline in -webkit-focus-ring-color. That is not the theme's focusBorder or contrastActiveBorder, unlike every other control.
proposal: Add a:focus-visible to the shared focus rule in primitives.css.

claim: README headings keep their Markdown level: a '#' renders an h1 inside the details region, under the pane's h2 package title. The markdown renderer has no heading override. The workbench shows an extension README in its own webview document.
proposal: Shift README headings by two levels (h1 to h3, capped at h6) in the marked renderer, or wrap the README in role=document.

claim: The search combobox does not describe its hidden keys: ArrowRight lists versions, ArrowLeft returns and Ctrl+Enter installs. The listboxes describe their keys with a hint, but the combobox has no aria-describedby, and the visual '›' affordance is aria-hidden.
proposal: Give SearchBox an optional hint rendered as a visually hidden description, as Listbox does.

claim: In Dark High Contrast, VS Code leaves list.activeSelectionBackground unset. nUIget draws selection only as that background, so a selected compact (sidebar) row probably has no mark other than the focus ring; comfortable rows keep the 3 px accent. This is a hypothesis about the rendered result, and the HC capture is ambiguous because of hover.
proposal: Add an HC outline for selected rows (contrastActiveBorder, dotted as the workbench does — workbench CSS not re-read) and capture the sidebar in HC with the pointer elsewhere.

claim: In Multi Install, the reason a project cannot be picked (centrally managed, unsupported, preview failed) is a sibling span that is not tied to the check box. Disabled check boxes are no tab stops, so keyboard and screen-reader users never meet the reason.
proposal: aria-describedby from the check box to the note; consider aria-disabled so blocked rows stay focusable.

claim: Hypotheses that only a screen reader can settle: the whole listbox is aria-busy while it revalidates, and so is a busy option, and some screen readers withhold busy content; warning and info banners are role=status regions mounted together with their text, which is often not announced.
proposal: Put both on the P7.4 checklist; meanwhile H1 snapshots record aria-busy per state.

claim: H4: a cheap jsdom guard. In every feature test that opens a Dialog or ConfirmDialog, assert that document.activeElement is not body after Confirm and after Cancel. The scratch probes reproduce finding 1 and serve as templates.
proposal: About 0.25 day, in InstalledTab, UpdatesTab, AllProjectsUpdates, UpdatesSection, SourcesControl and DetailsPane tests.

claim: H5: a runtime reduced-motion check. Set workbench.reduceMotion 'on' in the UI settings for one suite and assert body.vscode-reduce-motion plus zero running animations while a spinner and a skeleton are on screen. This depends on fixing finding 4. The OS path through CDP Emulation.setEmulatedMedia is a hypothesis, with the same iframe caveat as H1.
proposal: About 0.5 day after the token fix.

claim: H8: a rule-coverage ledger for the jsdom suite. Log each axe rule outcome through a setup file and fail when a rule in a committed 'must pass somewhere' list becomes inapplicable, so a pinned property cannot silently vanish. The scratch logger ran the unchanged 565 tests and produced the ledger.
proposal: About 0.25 day, behind an env flag in the frontend project.

claim: Wrong or unexpected versions (wildcard, empty, floating, semver, unlisted, prerelease) recur in 8 versions and are still a 2.0 gotcha.
proposal: Every control that writes a version shows the exact version it will write; this is already covered by the 'A webview install without a version' gotcha.

claim: 1.x moved toward workbench-native visuals five times (Extensions-style search, codicons and VS Code tokens, native progress and sash, Extensions-view funnel, native sidebar styling). The owner's memory records hitting the native TreeView blocker repeatedly. This confirms the owner's native-feeling direction.
proposal: No plan change. The sidebar dimension re-checks microsoft/vscode#161753 and the hybrid layout (not re-verified here).

claim: Reach numbers do not count users reliably. The current Marketplace listing starts on 2026-03-09 at 1.11.0, yet the CHANGELOG fixes Marketplace display in February, so the earlier listing history is unknown. GitHub clones come from CI. 83 installs is a lower bound since 2026-03-09.
proposal: Do not size or prioritise work by install counts. Record the baseline at the pre-release.

claim: Judged from the PNGs: they show the e2e test workspace, a 'Sign In' button, two-package lists, and in nuiget-updates.png half the frame is an empty details pane ('Select a package to see its details.') plus an unrelated 'nUIget: Restored 1 project.' toast. This is weak hero material next to peers' cropped feature shots.

The manifest has no qna, so the Marketplace Q & A tab is on: a second inbox for a solo maintainer (0 questions today). Peers redirect it: Jupyter to GitHub Discussions, C# Dev Kit to GitHub issues, Error Lens disables it (qna=false).
proposal: Set qna to the GitHub issues URL.

claim: The 14 keywords include five near-duplicates (package manager, package management, packages, nuget packages, manage nuget). None covers distinguishing features: central package management/CPM, vulnerabilities, csproj/fsproj/vbproj, transitive, PackageReference. The effect on search ranking is a hypothesis.

The Marketplace page JSON carries IsMDPruned/PrunedMDLength/OverviewMDLength, so a README pruning threshold exists. No measured page was pruned up to 37,135 bytes (GitLens); nUIget's README on main is 18,839 bytes. The threshold was not found.
The docs recommend a SUPPORT.md, but vsce 4.0.0 has no code for it; the Support link comes from bugs.url. nUIget has no SUPPORT.md, and whether the Marketplace reads one is not verified.
The README tip at line 84 ('Right-click a project in Solution Explorer') does not say that Solution Explorer is C# Dev Kit's view; the menu contribution is when view == solutionExplorer.
In CHANGELOG 2.0.0, '2.0 package sources' heads two different bullets (lines 30 and 57), and 50 bullets start with the noise prefix '2.0 '.

'Works with: Universal' is the Marketplace's normal label for desktop extensions (ESLint and Go show it too), yet CHANGELOG 1.2.1 records a 'fix' of it. The released entry describes no defect; leave it as released history.

Judged from the image: the icon (512x512 PNG, valid) shows a red/black throttle grip (hypothesis: 'gasrulle' is Swedish for throttle grip). It says nothing about packages or NuGet. The banner is the .NET purple #512BD4. It is the owner's brand, listed for the owner's decision.

A new browse text drops the previous results for a 3-row skeleton for the length of the search. The workbench Extensions view keeps the old list until the new model resolves and shows a view-container progress bar.
proposal: Keep the last answered results, busy under the progress bar, while a new text loads; use the skeleton only for the first search. Webview, 0.5 d. The owner decides whether 'previous data' may belong to another text.

claim: The sidebar asks transitive/metadata for its installed rows (measured) but no sidebar file reads metadata, so every sidebar start costs a host enrichment including the vulnerability download. The main panel's transitive prefetch also asks lite metadata for every transitive package while the section is collapsed.
proposal: Add a metadata flag on InstalledProvider, off in the sidebar like prefetch={false}. Ask transitive metadata on expand only, keeping the count prefetch. Webview, 0.5 d.

claim: Streamed update rows arrive bare (default icon, no authors) and are re-sorted by id on every found chunk, so rows shift under the pointer while the user may be aiming at an Update button. Icons and authors arrive only with the answer.
proposal: Append rows in arrival order and sort once at the answer, or hold the skeleton briefly. Webview only.

claim: Queued and running operations look identical on a row (same spinner and verb). The status bar says only 'nUIget: operation running', and a single operation opens no notification. The pinned 1.85 API offers ProgressOptions.location {viewId} (a native view progress bar) and ProgressLocation.Window with text.
proposal: In src/host/feedback.ts: a Window progress naming the package and project for single operations, and a {viewId} progress for the sidebar. Show 'Queued' on waiting rows. Rendering of {viewId} on a webview view is not verified.

claim: While the first list is provisional, the main panel shows rows and an info badge only: no progress bar, no busy header, no tab count. The sidebar announces 'Loading installed packages' while rows are visible. Busy cues are spread over header spinners, bars, badges, row spinners and the Refresh icon, where the workbench uses a single view progress bar.
proposal: One 'view is working' cue per surface (the progress bar) from first request to the authoritative answer. Reserve the badge for fidelity, not progress.

claim: Measured start order: the main panel posts sources/list before installed/get in the same commit (child-first effects), which is the order that triggers the accepted N72 double `dotnet nuget config paths` walk on every panel open. It competes with the walk the first rows wait on.
proposal: Reconsider together with the X-3 config-chain cache; N72 says P7.6 may reopen it.

claim: package/prewarm has a handler but no webview caller, and hover prefetch of details (MI11/MB13) is still open. For search the value is limited, because the start-up updates/get already resolves the project's service indexes.
proposal: Send package/prewarm on search-box focus (mainly a credential warm-up, N84). Do MI11 hover prefetch as designed in the parity audit.

claim: The informational benchmark job compares against a committed baseline that its own README calls single-machine only, and its summary prints only counts. Where the current baseline was recorded is not verified.
proposal: Re-record the baseline on the runner image, or compare within one run only.

claim: The computed task text of this sweep (not the owner's prompt file) calls the captures a 'VS Code 1.105-era build'. The UI job log of the capture commit (c50d335, run 39025149785) shows VS Code 1.140.0 and ChromeDriver 150.0.7871.124.
